title: Encode Number
statement: List every string made of the characters `0` and `1`, shorter strings first and strings of the same length in increasing binary order: `""`, `"0"`, `"1"`, `"00"`, `"01"`, `"10"`, `"11"`, `"000"`, and so on. The code of a non-negative integer `num` is the string at position `num` of this list, counting from 0. Return the code of `num`.
notes:
## Intuition

Count the strings before each length: 1 of length 0, 2 of length 1, 4 of length 2, so length `L` begins at position `2^L - 1`. Shift every position by one and length `L` covers `2^L` to `2^(L+1) - 1`: exactly the numbers whose binary form has `L + 1` digits. Inside that range, the order matches the binary order of the last `L` digits. So the code of `num` is the binary form of `num + 1` with its leading `1` removed. A slower route skips whole length groups one by one and then writes the offset with leading zeros.

## Approach

1. Set `value = num + 1` and start with an empty `code`.
2. While `value` has more than one binary digit (`value > 1`), put its lowest bit `value & 1` in front of `code`.
3. Shift `value` right by one to drop that bit.
4. When only the leading `1` is left, stop and return `code`.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = 23`, so `value = 24`, which is `11000` in binary. The loop reads the low bits 0, 0, 0, 1, building `"0"`, `"00"`, `"000"`, `"1000"`, while `value` goes 12, 6, 3, 1. With `value = 1` the loop ends, leaving `"1000"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log num): one step per binary digit.
- Space: O(log num) for the returned string.

## Pitfalls

- Writing `num` itself in binary is wrong: `num = 3` must give `"00"`, not `"11"`. Add 1 first.
- `num = 0` must return the empty string, which the loop gives because `value = 1` never enters it.
- Do not call `(num + 1).toString(2)` and forget to drop the first character.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `value` | `num + 1`, shifted right as its bits are read |
| `code` | the digits collected so far, lowest digit last |

narration.2: Shift by one: the code is the binary form of num + 1 without its leading 1.
narration.3: Start with no digits; they are added from the lowest bit up.
narration.5: Keep going while value has more digits than the leading 1.
narration.6: Put the lowest bit of value in front of the digits collected so far.
narration.7: Drop that bit by shifting value right.
narration.9: Only the leading 1 is left, so the collected digits are the code.
